#OTDwx: Typhoon Goni ‘15 (Ineng) impacted much of E Asia on its trek. Goni led to flooding in the Philippines causing major damage. Numerous were killed including miners in Mankayan. Impacts were also felt in Japan, the Korean Peninsula & Russia.

I’m not quite sure where I should properly say thank you, so please allow me to tag the team @cdmentph here. After the hi-touch, I accidentally missed a step and fell down the stairs. I couldn’t get up right away, but the staff rushed in to help me immediately. They kept monitoring me, checking if I was okay, if I could manage. Even though the accident was entirely my own fault. I felt so guilty for causing concern.

When I started feeling better, they still kindly advised me to get first aid until the very end of the event. The care I received was truly exceptional. The nurse was so gentle and friendly, treating me kindly even though I felt like such a burden.

Thank you so, so much.
Everyone was incredibly kind. I truly love the Philippines with all my heart. 😭💖

data.raw_text:
SCIENCE-BACKED SOLUTIONS FOR FLOODING

Iginiit ng geologist at disaster resilience expert na si Dr. Mahar Lagmay na hindi dapat limitado sa pagpapatayo lamang ng flood control infrastructures ang pamahalaan para matugunan ang problema sa baha.

Ayon kay Lagmay, ang executive director ng University of the Philippines Research Institute, mahalagang konsultahin muna ng mga lokal na pamahalaan at lalawigan ang mga siyentipiko para maiwasan ang pagpapatupad ng mga hindi epektibong flood control measure.

Kasunod ito ng mga usapin sa maanomalyang flood control projects na naiugnay sa umano’y katiwalian, kung saan malaking porsyento ng pondo umano ang napupunta sa mga opisyal ng pamahalaan, mambabatas, at contractors. | via https://t.co/95Yk9O7wUs
